a.notes: SELF-REPORT DISCREPANCY, not just undercounting: the agent's own final summary did not mention using grep for this task AT ALL, despite the runbook explicitly asking it to report exactly this. Transcript shows one Bash call: `grep -rn "func attachArgv" .../internal/ ; grep -n "attachArgv" .../run.go`, which is what actually located the dead call site at run.go:295. This grep use looks structurally justified (the deleted `attachArgv` free function no longer resolves as an LSP symbol at all -- textDocument_definition/references cannot return references to a symbol that no longer exists -- so a literal text search was the only way to find the stale call site), but the self-report's complete silence on it is the material problem, independent of whether the grep itself was reasonable.

_note: WARM-DAEMON, BLIND-AGENT experiment (2026-08-29, session 5cb8f382). Compare against: cold-daemon same-orchestrator run (9->4 tool_uses cold, 77.9s) AND this orchestrating session's own warm-but-INFORMED rerun (2 tool_uses, 13.8s, see scorecard.md) -- this blind run is dramatically slower than the informed warm run despite an identical warm daemon, which is the headline finding: daemon warmth alone did not reproduce the earlier speedup once a genuinely blind agent (more exploratory calls, an actual grep detour) was doing the work instead of an already-informed operator.
